I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou, that is the crop pattern I trust most because it matches the local weather, the irrigation conditions, and the machines I can easily hire. At my age, I do not want crops that need too much hand labor or too much market watching, so I will not plant vegetables, cotton, or anything fussy. I will finish the winter wheat that is already in the field, manage water and fertilizer steadily, and then after harvest I will go straight into summer maize on the same land. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I care about stable emergence and yield more than saving seed myself. I will keep fertilization moderate, not excessive, because I want a reliable harvest and I do not want to waste money. For tillage, I will keep it simple: rotary tillage for wheat preparation, then no-tillage or very light direct seeding for maize after wheat so I can save labor and catch the season on time. I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, and I will spray only as needed for the main local pests and diseases. That is the system I would run this year because it is familiar, practical, and manageable for me.
